name: Seven-Day Money Magnet Jar Candle
description: Tall glass-jar candles, often called seven-day or novena candles, are a staple of hoodoo candle work and Catholic folk devotion in the Americas, and candle shops still 'fix' them for customers by carving the top and adding oil and herbs. Their long, steady burn suits a slow, building money-drawing working. Here the candle is lit in daily sessions and snuffed between them, so each relighting renews the call for income.

ingredients.item: Green glass-jar 7-day candle (about 8 inches tall), unscented
Small square of paper and a pen
Salt water and a soft cloth, for cleansing

steps: Cleanse the outside of the jar by wiping it with a cloth dampened in salt water, and dry it well.
With the skewer, carve a dollar sign, your initials and the amount you need into the top surface of the wax, working away from your hand and keeping the marks a little away from the wick.
Dress the candle with three drops of Money Drawing Oil placed on the wax near the glass rim, never on the wick, and blot any pooling with a tissue.
Sprinkle a very small pinch of the ground Cinnamon and Basil on the wax near the rim, well away from the wick, so it sits like a ring of dust rather than a heap.
Write your money petition on the paper and slide it under the heatproof tile, then set the jar on top with the Pyrite beside it.
Light the candle and say the chant while picturing money arriving through work, sales and fair dealings.
Let it burn for one to three hours while you are home and awake, then close by snuffing it with a snuffer or the jar lid and saying 'This work rests, and does not end.'
Relight it at the same time each day, repeating the chant, until about half an inch of wax remains.
howToUse: Burn the candle in daily sessions; it is named for its roughly seven days of continuous burn, so in short sessions it may last several weeks, and that is fine. Watch for real-world openings and act on them. When you stop with half an inch of wax left, let the jar cool completely, scrape out the leftover wax and herbs, wrap them with the petition in a scrap of paper and bury them near your front door or put them in the trash on your way out of the house. Wash the jar and recycle it or use it as a coin jar, and keep the Pyrite in your wallet or cash box.
chant:
Green flame, steady flame,
call my money, speak my name.
Day by day the glass grows bright,
bring me plenty, fair and right.
intention: I draw steady money to me through honest work and good opportunity, day by day.
timing: Start on a Thursday or Sunday during the waxing moon; relight daily at the same hour.
bestTime: Any season; a good start for a new month, quarter or financial year.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Glass-jar candles can crack when hot: set the jar on a heatproof surface, never in a window, and stop burning it when about half an inch of wax remains so it never burns dry. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, keep it off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, and wash your hands afterward; too much oil can make the flame flare. Formula oils and essential oils must be diluted (a few drops in a teaspoon of carrier oil) and never used on broken skin. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Herbs on top of a jar candle can flare: use only a small pinch of finely ground herb near the glass, never near the wick, and watch it the whole time; if anything catches, cover the jar with its lid or a snuffer. Cinnamon can irritate skin, so wash your hands after handling it. Keep the Pyrite away from small children, who could choke on it. Ventilate the room, keep a snuffer or lid and a bowl of water nearby, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let the wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep the candle, oil, Cinnamon and Pyrite away from pets; cinnamon can irritate a pet's mouth and skin, and cats are especially sensitive to essential oils.

name: Coin Circle Prosperity Taper
description: Coins appear in money charms across many folk traditions, from silver dimes carried for luck in American folk magic to coins set out at the New Year to invite prosperity. In this candle working a green taper stands in the center of a ring of coins, so its light 'warms' the money around it. The coins are then kept and carried so they can go out and call more money back.

ingredients.item: Salt water in a small bowl

steps: Cleanse the coins by swishing them in the salt water, then rinse and dry them; wipe the taper with a dry cloth.
With a pin, carve a circle near the base of the taper and the word 'Return' running up the lower half, carving away from your hand.

Dress the taper by rubbing two or three drops of Prosperity Oil onto the lower half of the taper only, stroking from the bottom up to draw, then wipe off any excess and keep oil off the wick and the top part of the candle.
Set the taper firmly in its holder in the center of the heatproof plate and lay the coins heads up in a circle around it, at least two inches from the holder.
Sprinkle a fine line of Allspice in a ring just outside the coins and set the Green Aventurine at the top of the circle.
Light the taper and say the chant once for each coin, touching each one in turn, clockwise.
Let it burn for one hour while you sit with it, then close by snuffing it and saying 'Coin to coin, the circle holds.' Repeat for two more evenings or until the taper is finished.
howToUse: Leave the coins in their circle between sessions. When the taper has burned down or you have finished three sessions, let everything cool, then put the coins in your wallet, purse or a money jar; spend one coin within a week as a 'messenger' and keep the rest. Peel the leftover wax off the holder once it is fully cool, wrap it in paper and keep it in the money jar or a drawer where you keep bills, or bin it with thanks. Carry the Green Aventurine for luck in money matters, and sweep up the Allspice and put it in the trash.
chant:
Round and round the silver goes,
where the light falls, money grows.
What I spend comes home to me,
coin by coin, so mote it be.
intention: I warm my money with light so it circulates freely and returns to me multiplied.
timing: Thursday (Jupiter) during the waxing moon; or the first day of a month.
bestTime: Any season; New Year's Eve and the first of the month are traditional for money work.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Tapers can drip and lean: make sure the holder grips the taper upright and keep the coins, stone and spice well clear of drips. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, keep it off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, and wash your hands afterward; too much oil can make the flame flare. Formula oils and essential oils must be diluted (a few drops in a teaspoon of carrier oil) and never used on broken skin. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Allspice can irritate skin and eyes, so wash your hands after handling it and keep the ring well away from the flame. Coins and small stones are a choking hazard for young children, so pick them all up after each session if children are around. Ventilate the room, keep a snuffer or lid and a bowl of water nearby, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let the wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep the candle, oil, coins and spice out of reach of pets; swallowed coins (especially US pennies made after 1982, which contain zinc) can cause zinc poisoning in dogs, and cats are especially sensitive to essential oils.

name: Business Blessing Candle Trio
description: Shopkeepers in many traditions bless their premises at opening time, and in modern candle magic three colors are often combined so each does one job. This trio uses a green pillar for income, a gold or yellow pillar for success and visibility, and a white pillar for blessing and protection, set in a triangle around a business card or a sign from your business. It suits a new venture, a slow season or a fresh start after a setback.

ingredients.item: Green pillar candle (about 3 x 4 inches), unscented
Gold or yellow pillar candle (about 3 x 4 inches), unscented
White pillar candle (about 3 x 4 inches), unscented
Business card, receipt or logo printout

steps: Cleanse the space by sweeping or wiping the counter, desk or table where the candles will stand, then wipe each pillar with a dry cloth.

With a toothpick, carve your business name into the green pillar, a star or crown into the gold pillar, and an equal-armed cross or circle into the white pillar, all on the lower half and away from your hand.
Dress each pillar with two or three drops of its own oil (Money Drawing Oil on green, Crown of Success Oil on gold, Blessing Oil on white) on the lower half only, wiping off the excess.
Set the three pillars in a triangle on the tray, each at least three inches from the others, with the business card face up in the center and the Citrine on top of it.
Lay one Bay Laurel leaf flat on the tray in front of each candle, at least two inches from its base.
Light the white candle first for blessing, then the green for money, then the gold for success, speaking the matching line of the chant as you light each.
Burn them together for 30 minutes to an hour while you work nearby, then snuff them in reverse order and say 'Blessed be this work and all who come here.' Repeat on each business day for a week.
howToUse: Relight the trio at opening time or at the start of your work session, never when no one is there to watch it. After a week, or when the pillars are low, let the wax cool completely and keep a small piece of each color wrapped with the three bay leaves in a paper packet in your till, cash drawer or desk. Bin the rest of the wax with thanks. Keep the Citrine on the business card near the register or your workspace.
chant:
White for blessing, keep us whole,
green for money, fill the bowl,
gold for success that all can see:
this work is blessed, so mote it be.
intention: I bless my business with protection, steady income and visible success.
timing: Start on a Thursday or Sunday morning during the waxing moon, ideally at opening time.
bestTime: Any season; at a grand opening, a new quarter or before a busy season.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Three flames give off more heat and soot than one, so space the pillars apart and never set the tray near shelving, signage, paper stock or a customer area where people could brush past. Check your lease or workplace rules first, since many businesses do not allow open flames; if so, do the spell at home with a business card. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, keep it off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, and wash your hands afterward; too much oil can make the flame flare. Formula oils and essential oils must be diluted (a few drops in a teaspoon of carrier oil) and never used on broken skin. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Keep the bay leaves flat on the tray well away from the flames, as dry leaves catch fire easily. Ventilate the room, keep a snuffer or lid and a bowl of water nearby, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let the wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep shop cats and other pets away from the candles and oils; bay laurel is listed by the ASPCA as toxic to cats and dogs, and cats are especially sensitive to essential oils.

name: Lucky Break Orange Candle
description: In modern candle-color lore, orange stands for opportunity, sudden change and luck that moves quickly, and 'fast luck' formulas are sold in hoodoo-inspired candle shops for exactly that purpose. This working marks an orange taper into three sections so it can be burned over three days, each section opening a little more room for a lucky break. Use it when you need a chance, a callback or a door to open.

ingredients.item: Orange Peel, dried and finely ground
Bowl of water with a pinch of salt, for cleansing

steps: Cleanse yourself by washing your hands in the salt water, then wipe the taper with a dry cloth.
With a pin, carve two rings around the taper to divide it into three equal sections, and carve a small arrow pointing up in each section, carving away from your hand.
Dress the lower section only with two or three drops of Fast Luck Oil, stroking upward, and wipe off any excess.
Roll the lower two inches of the oiled taper very lightly in the ground Orange Peel so it holds only a thin dusting, then tap off anything loose.
Fix the taper in its holder on the heatproof plate and scatter the Chamomile in a ring around the holder, with the stone in front.
Light the candle, say the chant three times and name the break you are hoping for.

Let it burn down to the first carved ring, then snuff it and close by saying 'One door opens.' On the second and third days, burn to the next ring, closing with 'Two doors open' and 'Every door opens.'
howToUse: On each of the three days, take one practical step toward your break: send the email, make the call, enter the contest. After the third session, when the wax is completely cool, collect the drips and the leftover stub, wrap them in a scrap of paper with a pinch of the Chamomile and carry it in your bag until your luck arrives, then bury it or bin it with thanks. Keep the stone in your pocket for important days.
chant:
Orange flame, quick and bright,
turn my luck toward the light.
One, two, three, the doors swing wide,
a lucky break is on my side.
intention: I open myself to a fast, fortunate break and I am ready to take it.
timing: Start on a Wednesday or Thursday during the waxing moon.
bestTime: Any season; especially before an audition, an application deadline or a big decision.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, keep it off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, and wash your hands afterward; too much oil can make the flame flare. Formula oils and essential oils must be diluted (a few drops in a teaspoon of carrier oil) and never used on broken skin. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Rolling candles in herbs is a fire risk: use only a thin dusting of finely ground Orange Peel on the lower two inches, never near the top, and watch the flame the whole time. Keep the Chamomile ring on the plate well clear of the flame. Chamomile can cause allergic reactions in people sensitive to ragweed, daisies or marigolds, so handle it with care if you have those allergies. Ventilate the room, keep a snuffer or lid and a bowl of water nearby, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let the wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Chamomile and orange peel are listed by the ASPCA as toxic to cats and dogs; keep the candle, herbs and oil away from pets, and remember cats are especially sensitive to essential oils.

name: Three-Light Job Interview Layout
description: Candle layouts, where several candles are arranged to stand for people and goals, are common in hoodoo and modern candle magic. In this one a small human figure candle stands for you, flanked by a yellow chime candle for clear speech and a green chime candle for the job offer. It is done the evening before an interview, alongside real preparation, to steady your nerves and set a clear intention.

ingredients.item: Human figure candle (about 4-6 inches), in white or a color you feel represents you
Copy of the job listing or the company name on paper

steps: Cleanse the candles by passing each one through the steam of a cup of hot water or wiping it with a cloth, and cleanse yourself by washing your hands and face.
With a toothpick, carve your name on the back of the figure candle, the word 'Clear' on the yellow chime and the job title or company name on the green chime, carving away from your hand.
Dress all three with a drop or two of Road Opener Oil, on the lower half of the chimes and on the legs and body of the figure only, keeping oil off the wicks and heads, and wipe off any excess.

Place the job listing on the tray with the figure candle standing on a small heatproof saucer on top of it, the yellow chime on its left and the green chime on its right, each about four inches apart.
Sprinkle the Cinquefoil in a ring around the outer edge of the tray, well away from the flames, and set the Tiger's Eye in front of the figure.
Light the yellow chime, then the green chime, then the figure candle, and say the chant. Rehearse your answers to likely questions out loud while the candles burn.
Let the two chimes burn all the way down while you stay in the room (about two hours). Burn the figure for 15 minutes only, then snuff it and say 'I walk in ready.'
howToUse: Carry the Tiger's Eye to the interview. After the interview, relight the figure candle for 15 minutes to give thanks, whatever the outcome, and repeat each evening until you hear back or the figure is spent. Once all the wax is completely cool, collect the chime candle stubs, a little of the figure's leftover wax and the Cinquefoil, wrap them in the job listing and keep the bundle in your bag or desk until you have an answer; then bury it if you got the job, or bin it with thanks and start a new layout for the next opportunity.
chant:
Yellow for words both clear and true,
green for the work I'm meant to do,
and here I stand between the two:
I walk in ready, I walk through.
intention: I speak clearly and confidently in my interview and draw the job that is right for me.
timing: The evening before the interview; Wednesday (Mercury) is ideal for communication.
bestTime: Any season; whenever an interview is booked.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Figure candles burn unevenly and can drip a lot of wax, so stand the figure on its own heatproof saucer and never leave it lit for long periods. Chime candles burn quickly and get very hot near the end: keep the holders on the tray and stay with them until they are fully out. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, keep it off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, and wash your hands afterward; too much oil can make the flame flare. Formula oils and essential oils must be diluted (a few drops in a teaspoon of carrier oil) and never used on broken skin. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Keep the Cinquefoil ring and the paper well clear of drips and flames. Ventilate the room, keep a snuffer or lid and a bowl of water nearby, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let the wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep pets out of the room while three flames are burning, and store the oil sealed; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils.

name: Black-to-Green Debt Turning Candle
description: Double-action candles, made in two colors with one layered over the other, are sold in many candle shops for work that removes one thing and brings in another. This working uses a black-over-green candle: the black top burns away debt, worry and money blocks, and once the flame reaches the green, the work turns to drawing in money and stability. It is a companion to practical steps such as a budget or a payment plan, not a substitute for them.

ingredients.item: Double-action black-over-green pillar candle (about 2 x 6 inches); or a black chime candle and a green chime candle (4 inches each)
A recent bill or a slip of paper listing your debts
Heatproof plate and a separate heatproof saucer

steps: Cleanse the candle by wiping it with a cloth and passing it over the salt; cleanse yourself by washing your hands in salt water.
With a toothpick, carve a minus sign and the word 'Debt' into the black part, and a plus sign and the word 'Paid' into the green part, carving away from your hand.

Dress the black part with two drops of Uncrossing Oil, stroking from the middle out toward the top to push debt away, and the green part with two drops of Money Drawing Oil, stroking from the bottom toward the middle to draw. Keep oil off the wick and the top half inch, and wipe off the excess.
Set the candle on the heatproof plate, sprinkle the salt in a ring around it, and sprinkle the Patchouli in a second ring just outside the salt. Place the Smoky Quartz on the bill beside the plate.
Light the candle and say the first two lines of the chant. Sit with it for an hour, writing down one practical step you can take toward the debt, then snuff it.
Relight it daily until the black is gone. When the flame reaches the green, tear the bill or list in half, put it on the saucer under the Smoky Quartz, and switch to the last two lines of the chant.
Keep relighting until the candle is finished or about an inch remains, and close each session by snuffing it and saying 'What I owe grows less; what I hold grows more.'
howToUse: If you use two chime candles instead, burn the black one fully first, then light the green one from a match on the next day. Make at least one payment, call or budget change during the working. When the candle is done and cool, gather the black drips and bin them off your property to take the debt away. Keep a little of the green wax wrapped with the Patchouli in your wallet or bill folder. Shred and recycle the torn bill, and put the salt in the trash.
chant:
Black burns down and debt grows small,
what I owe I loose from all.
Green burns up and plenty grows,
steady as the river flows.
intention: I release the weight of debt and turn my finances toward stability and plenty.
timing: Begin the black during the waning moon and aim to reach the green near the new moon; Saturday to start.
bestTime: Any season; after the holidays or at tax time are traditional moments to take stock.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, keep it off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, and wash your hands afterward; too much oil can make the flame flare. Formula oils and essential oils must be diluted (a few drops in a teaspoon of carrier oil) and never used on broken skin. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Black candle dyes can produce more visible soot, so trim the wick to about a quarter inch before each lighting and keep the room ventilated. Keep the paper well away from the flame and do not burn it. Salt kills plants and can mark some surfaces, so keep it on the plate. If debt is causing serious stress, a nonprofit credit counselor can help alongside this spell. Ventilate the room, keep a snuffer or lid and a bowl of water nearby, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let the wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep pets away from the candle and the salt ring; salt licked up by pets can cause salt poisoning, and cats are especially sensitive to essential oils.

name: Plenty Pillar on a Bay Leaf Petition
description: Bay laurel was sacred to Apollo in ancient Greece, and writing wishes on bay leaves is a popular modern folk practice. In this working, three bay leaves carry a written petition for abundance and are laid under the heatproof plate that holds a green pillar candle, so the candle 'stands on' your request without the leaves ever touching the flame. The pillar is burned once a week until it is finished, letting abundance build slowly.

ingredients.item: Green pillar candle (about 3 x 6 inches), unscented
Bay Laurel leaves, dried and whole
Heatproof plate larger than the candle base

steps: Cleanse the candle and leaves by wiping the candle with a dry cloth and passing it and the leaves through the light of a sunny window, saying 'Clean and clear.'
With the marker, write one word of your petition on each bay leaf, such as 'Plenty', 'Ease' and 'Enough', and lay them in a triangle on the table.
Set the heatproof plate on top of the leaves so they are completely covered and protected.
With a toothpick, carve a spiral that winds upward around the lower half of the pillar, carving away from your hand.
Dress the lower half with three drops of Prosperity Oil, wipe off the excess, and dust the lowest inch very lightly with ground Cinnamon, tapping off anything loose.
Stand the pillar in the center of the plate, set the three Cloves on the plate in front of it and the stone behind it.
Light the candle and say the chant. Burn it for one hour, then snuff it, saying 'Plenty grows while the light rests.' Relight it once a week on the same day until the pillar is finished.
howToUse: Burn the pillar weekly, never longer than you can watch it. Pillars tend to tunnel, so after each session, once the wax is soft but not hot, gently press the outer rim inward. When it is finished or too low to burn safely, let it cool, then wrap the leftover wax with the three bay leaves and Cloves in paper and keep the packet in your kitchen or wherever you keep your money until the next new moon, then bury it under a plant or bin it with thanks. Keep the stone near your bills.
chant:
Three green leaves beneath the light,
plenty rising day and night.
Enough for me and some to share,
abundance gathers everywhere.
intention: I invite steady, growing abundance into my life, with enough for me and enough to share.
timing: Thursday during the waxing moon; relight every Thursday.
bestTime: Any season; especially late summer and autumn harvest time.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Never put the bay leaves directly under or beside the candle: they stay beneath the plate where no flame or hot wax can reach them. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, keep it off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, and wash your hands afterward; too much oil can make the flame flare. Formula oils and essential oils must be diluted (a few drops in a teaspoon of carrier oil) and never used on broken skin. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Use only a thin dusting of Cinnamon on the lowest inch; rolling a candle heavily in herbs is a fire risk. Cinnamon and clove can irritate skin, so wash your hands after handling them. Ventilate the room, keep a snuffer or lid and a bowl of water nearby, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let the wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Bay laurel is listed by the ASPCA as toxic to cats and dogs, and cinnamon and clove can irritate pets; keep the candle, leaves, spices and oil out of reach, and remember cats are especially sensitive to essential oils.

name: Sunday Gold Sun Candle for Success
description: In the traditional system of planetary days, Sunday belongs to the Sun, which rules success, recognition, vitality and leadership, and gold and yellow are its colors. This working dresses a gold pillar with a carved sun sign and sets it in a ring of sunflower seeds and marigold petals, lit in the morning to borrow the energy of the rising day. Use it for a goal you want to see shine: a launch, an award, a performance review or a personal achievement.

ingredients.item: Gold or yellow pillar candle (about 3 x 4 inches), unscented
Sunflower seeds, unsalted, in the shell

steps: Cleanse yourself at sunrise on Sunday by washing your face and hands with cool water and opening a window to let fresh air and daylight into the room.
Write your goal on the paper as if it has already happened, and set it under the heatproof plate.
With a toothpick, carve the sun sign (a circle with a dot in the center) on the front of the pillar and your initials beneath it, carving away from your hand.
Dress the lower half of the pillar with three drops of Crown of Success Oil, stroking upward toward the sun sign, and wipe off any excess.
Stand the pillar on the plate and lay the Sunflower seeds and Calendula petals in a ring around it, at least two inches from the base, with the stone at the top like a rising sun.
Light the candle, face the east or the brightest window, and say the chant three times.

Let it burn for 30 to 60 minutes while you plan the next real step toward your goal, then close by snuffing it and saying 'The sun goes on.' Relight it each Sunday until the goal is reached or the candle is spent.
howToUse: Relight the candle every Sunday morning, taking one visible action toward your goal each week. When it is finished, let the wax cool completely, then break off a small piece of the gold wax and keep it with the stone on your desk or in your work bag as a reminder of your success. Bin the rest of the wax with thanks, and scatter the Sunflower seeds and Calendula outdoors for the birds and the soil.
chant:
Sun of Sunday, gold and high,
lift my name into the sky.
What I aim for, let it shine;
the crown of my success is mine.
intention: I shine in my work and my efforts are seen, rewarded and successful.
timing: Sunday at sunrise or in the first hour after; waxing to full moon.
bestTime: Summer, especially near Midsummer, or any time you need recognition.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Keep the candle out of direct sun on a windowsill, which can soften or warp the pillar, and never set a lit candle in a window near curtains. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, keep it off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, and wash your hands afterward; too much oil can make the flame flare. Formula oils and essential oils must be diluted (a few drops in a teaspoon of carrier oil) and never used on broken skin. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Keep the seed and petal ring well clear of the flame and wax drips. Calendula is in the daisy family and may cause allergic reactions in people sensitive to ragweed, daisies or chrysanthemums. Ventilate the room, keep a snuffer or lid and a bowl of water nearby, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let the wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep pets away from the candle and oil; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, and seed shells can upset a pet's stomach if eaten.

name: Steady Work Brown Tealights
description: Brown is linked in candle-color lore with the earth, stability and practical matters, and 'steady work' formulas are sold in hoodoo-inspired shops for keeping a job and staying in good standing. This working uses a small brown tealight each workday morning for one working week, so the spell becomes a quiet daily habit rather than one big ritual. Each tealight burns for a short, watched session before you leave for work or log on.

ingredients.item: Brown tealight candles in metal or clear cups, unscented
Oak leaf, dried, or a small piece of oak bark
Work badge, business card or a slip of paper with your job title
Salt water and a cloth, for cleansing

steps: On Sunday evening, cleanse the five tealights by wiping their cups with a cloth dampened in salt water, and set them in a row on a shelf.
Pop each tealight out of its cup and, with a toothpick, carve a small square (for a solid foundation) into the underside of the wax, carving away from your hand.
Dress each tealight with a single drop of Steady Work Oil on the underside only, wipe off the excess and press it back into its cup, so the oil stays well away from the wick.

Each workday morning, set one tealight on the heatproof saucer on top of your badge or job slip, with the Oak leaf and stone beside the saucer and a pinch of Thyme in a ring on the saucer around the cup.
Light it, say the chant, and spend a few minutes planning one thing you will do well that day.
Let it burn while you get ready (at least 15 minutes, never while you are out of the room), then snuff it and say 'Steady as the oak, I stay.'
Relight the same tealight in the evening if you like, and use a fresh one each morning until all five are spent.
howToUse: Repeat the five-tealight week whenever your job feels uncertain, such as during layoffs, reviews or a new manager's arrival. Once each tealight has cooled completely, pop the leftover wax disc out of its cup; keep the five discs together with the Oak leaf in a small paper bag in your work bag or desk drawer, and bin them with thanks at the end of the month. Recycle the metal cups. Keep the stone at your workstation.
chant:
Brown as earth and firm as stone,
this work I do, this place I own.
Steady hand and steady pay,
here I'm valued, here I stay.
intention: I keep my job, do it well and am valued for the steady work I bring.
timing: Monday through Friday mornings, starting on a Monday; any moon phase, with waxing best.
bestTime: Any season; especially before reviews, contract renewals or times of workplace change.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Tealight cups get very hot: never move a lit or freshly snuffed tealight, and always set it on a heatproof saucer rather than directly on furniture. Never leave it burning while you shower, dress in another room or leave the house. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, keep it off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, and wash your hands afterward; too much oil can make the flame flare. Formula oils and essential oils must be diluted (a few drops in a teaspoon of carrier oil) and never used on broken skin. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Keep the Thyme ring on the saucer only and the Oak leaf and paper away from the flame. Ventilate the room, keep a snuffer or lid and a bowl of water nearby, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let the wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep pets away from the tealight and oil; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, and a curious pet can knock over a small, hot tealight.

name: Chime Candle Wish in One Sitting
description: Chime candles are small four-inch candles, originally made for spinning chime ornaments, that burn in about two hours and have become a favorite in modern candle magic for quick wishes. Because a chime is meant to burn all the way down in one sitting, this spell asks you to stay with it the entire time, which turns the wait into a focused meditation on your goal. Pick the color that fits your success wish.

ingredients.item: Chime candle (4 inches): green for money, orange for opportunity, yellow or gold for success
Strip of paper and a pen

steps: Cleanse the chime by holding it under your breath and blowing gently along its length three times (not at a flame), saying 'Only my wish lives here.'
Write your wish in one short sentence on the strip of paper and slide it under the heatproof plate.
With a pin, carve one key word from your wish down the side of the chime, carving away from your hand.
Dress the chime with one or two drops of oil on the lower half only, wipe off the excess, and set it in its holder on the plate.
Place the Star Anise and Clear Quartz on the plate, at least two inches from the holder.
Light the chime, say the chant, and set a timer for every 20 minutes to check the flame and restate your wish.
Stay in the room until the flame goes out on its own (about two hours), then close by saying 'My wish is sent; I go to meet it.'
howToUse: If you must leave before it finishes, snuff it and relight it as soon as you can, finishing the spell in a later sitting. Once the holder and wax are completely cool, peel off the leftover drips and wrap them with the paper wish and the Star Anise; keep the little bundle on your altar or in a drawer until the wish comes true, then bury it in the earth with thanks. If nothing has moved in a month, bin it and cast a fresh wish. Keep the Clear Quartz to charge the next one.
chant:
Little flame, burn straight and true,
carry my wish the whole night through.
When the last of you is gone,
my wish is sent and carries on.
intention: I send one clear wish for success into the world and I am ready to receive it.
timing: Any evening during the waxing moon; Thursday for money, Sunday for success, Wednesday for opportunity.
bestTime: Any season; a good choice for New Year's Eve or a birthday.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Chime candles are thin and burn hot near the end; use a holder made for chimes, set on a heatproof plate, and stay with the candle until it is completely out. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, keep it off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, and wash your hands afterward; too much oil can make the flame flare. Formula oils and essential oils must be diluted (a few drops in a teaspoon of carrier oil) and never used on broken skin. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Keep the Star Anise and stone well away from the flame. Do not eat the Star Anise afterward, since it has been near oils and wax. Ventilate the room, keep a snuffer or lid and a bowl of water nearby, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let the wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep pets out of the room while the chime burns and store the oil sealed; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils.

name: Lodestone Customer-Drawing Candle
description: Lodestones, naturally magnetic pieces of magnetite, have been carried as charms to draw luck, money and people for centuries, and in hoodoo they are traditionally 'fed' with magnetic sand (fine iron filings) to keep them strong. This working pairs a lodestone with a yellow pillar candle for attraction and visibility, so the candle's light draws customers and clients while the lodestone 'holds' them. It is best for shops, freelancers, online sellers and anyone who needs more people walking through the door.

ingredients.item: Yellow pillar candle (about 2 x 6 inches), unscented
Business card, shop sign, or a screenshot of your online store printed on paper

steps: Cleanse the lodestone by rinsing it briefly in cool water and drying it completely, and wipe the candle with a dry cloth.
With a toothpick, carve a horseshoe-magnet shape (a U) on the front of the pillar with arrows pointing into it, and your business name beneath, carving away from your hand.
Dress the lower half of the pillar with three drops of Lodestone Oil, stroking from the bottom toward you to draw, and wipe off the excess.
Set the pillar on the heatproof plate on top of your business card or printout, and mix the Basil and Sugar in a ring around the base, at least two inches out.
Put the lodestone on its own small dish beside the plate, rub a drop of the oil onto it, and 'feed' it a pinch of magnetic sand while saying 'Draw them in.'
Light the candle and say the chant, picturing a steady stream of happy customers arriving.
Burn it for 30 to 60 minutes during your business hours, then snuff it and say 'Doors stay open.' Relight it each business day, feeding the lodestone a pinch of sand once a week.
howToUse: Keep the fed lodestone near your register, front door, or the device you use to take orders. When the candle is finished, let the wax cool completely, then crumble a little of it with the Basil and Sugar mixture into a paper packet and tuck it under your doormat or behind the shop sign; bin the rest with thanks. Keep feeding the lodestone weekly on Friday and give it a drop of oil at each new moon.
chant:
Stone that pulls and flame that calls,
bring the people through my walls.
One by one and two by two,
customers come, and come back too.
intention: I draw a steady stream of good customers who are glad to buy from me and return.
timing: Friday or Thursday during the waxing moon; relight at opening time.
bestTime: Any season; especially before a launch, a sale or the holiday shopping season.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Check your lease or workplace rules before burning a candle at a business. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, keep it off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, and wash your hands afterward; too much oil can make the flame flare. Formula oils and essential oils must be diluted (a few drops in a teaspoon of carrier oil) and never used on broken skin. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Keep magnetic sand away from eyes, phones, cards and electronics, wash your hands after handling it, and keep it sealed. Lodestones and iron filings are a choking and swallowing hazard for children. Keep the sugar and basil ring well clear of the flame, as sugar burns hot if it catches. Ventilate the room, keep a snuffer or lid and a bowl of water nearby, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let the wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep pets away from the candle, oil, magnetic sand and sugar ring; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils.

name: Bathside Pink Chime Candle Self-Love Ritual
description: Candlelit baths are a much-loved modern witchcraft practice for self-care, and pink is widely used in contemporary candle magic for gentle, tender love, including love for yourself. In this ritual a small pink chime candle is carved with words you need to hear, dressed with self-love oil, and set beside the tub (never in it) while you soak in a simple salt and rose bath. The candle keeps watch while you practice speaking kindly to yourself.

ingredients.item: Pink chime candle (4 inch, about 2 hours burn time)
Love Me Now Self-Love Oil (or 2 drops Rose Geranium Essential Oil in 1 tsp Sweet Almond Oil)

ingredients.amount: a pinch for the plate, a handful for the bath bag

steps: Cleanse the candle by passing it through the steam of your running bath or wiping it with a cloth dampened in salt water, saying, 'Only love remains.' Let it dry.
With the toothpick, carving away from your hand, write three short words you want to feel down the side of the candle, such as 'worthy', 'soft' and 'whole'.
Dress the candle with three drops of oil, stroking from the middle down to the base only, keeping oil off the wick and the top half inch, then wipe off any excess and wash your hands.

Put the candle in its holder on the heatproof plate and set it on a flat, stable surface beside the bath, such as a closed counter or a stool, at least 12 inches from towels and curtains and out of reach of splashing water. Never set it on the tub rim or in the water. Scatter a pinch of crumbled Rose in a ring on the plate, 3 inches from the flame.
Fill the muslin bag with the salt and a handful of Rose petals, tie it shut and drop it into the warm (not hot) bath so no loose petals clog the drain.
Light the candle, step into the bath holding the Rose Quartz over your heart, and speak the chant three times, then read each carved word aloud as 'I am...'.
Soak for 15 to 20 minutes, looking at the flame and naming one thing you appreciate about yourself for each breath you count.
Close by thanking yourself aloud. Step out carefully, dry off, and snuff the candle before leaving the room.
howToUse: Repeat the bath once a week, relighting the same chime candle each time until it is used up, or let a fresh candle burn to the end on a later evening while you sit with it. Keep the Rose Quartz by your mirror. Once the leftover wax is completely cool, wrap it in a tissue with the crumbled Rose and keep it in your dresser drawer as a reminder of the promise you made to yourself, or bury it under a flowering plant. Empty the bath bag into the compost.
chant:
Pink as dawn and soft as rose,
kindness to myself now flows.
Every part of me is whole,
loved in body, loved in soul.
intention: I treat myself with the same tenderness I give the people I love.
timing: Friday (Venus) evening, waxing moon; the hour of Venus if you follow planetary hours.
bestTime: Any season; especially comforting in late winter or after a hard week.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) whenever you step away and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Keep the candle on a stable surface beside the bath, well away from towels and splashing water; never on the tub rim, never in the water, and never doze off in the bath while it burns. Bathroom floors are slippery, so step out carefully. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands after dressing, and never use essential oils undiluted or on broken skin. Do not add essential oils straight to bath water, since they do not mix with water and can irritate skin; keep them in the candle oil only. Keep the bath warm rather than hot, and skip it if you are pregnant, have heart or blood pressure problems, or feel faint in hot water. Keep the herb ring on the plate at least 3 inches from the flame and watch it the whole time, since dried plant material catches fire easily. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, keep a lid or snuffer and water nearby, and smother a wax fire with a lid; never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, and even diffused or spilled oil can harm them. Keep pets out of the bathroom while the candle is lit.

name: Two Figure Candle Harmony Spell
description: Figure candles shaped like people are widely used in hoodoo and modern candle magic to stand for the people in a working, and couple candles are a common choice for relationship work. This spell is for an existing couple who both agree to do it together: each partner dresses a figure candle that represents themselves, and the two are set facing each other to burn in short sessions while you talk. It asks for harmony, patience and kind communication between two willing people, never for control of either one.

ingredients.item: Figure candles in pink or white (about 6 inches), one representing each partner, chosen by each person
Peaceful Home Oil (or 3 drops Lavender Essential Oil in 1 tsp Jojoba Oil)
Salt water in a small bowl and a soft cloth

steps: Sit together and agree, out loud, that you both want this harmony working and what you each hope it brings, such as calmer arguments or more patience. If either of you is unsure, do not do the spell.
Cleanse each figure candle by wiping it with the cloth dampened in salt water, then pat it dry.

Each partner takes their own candle and, carving away from the hand with the toothpick, writes their own first name on the back and one quality they promise to bring, such as 'listening', on the front.

Each partner dresses their own candle with two or three drops of oil, stroking from the shoulders down to the feet only, keeping oil off the head, wick and top half inch. Wipe off the excess and wash your hands.

Stand the candles on the tray facing each other about 4 inches apart, with the Rose Quartz and Rhodonite between their feet, and scatter a ring of Lavender and Rose on the tray at least 3 inches from either flame.
Light each other's candle. Holding hands, speak the chant together, then each say one thing you appreciate about the other.
Let the candles burn for 20 to 30 minutes while you talk about something you would like to do together, then snuff them together.
howToUse: Relight the candles together for 20 to 30 minutes on six more evenings, moving them a little closer each night until they touch, and snuff them together each time. Figure candles often burn unevenly, so keep watching and trim any runaway wick. When they are finished, let the wax cool fully, gather the leftover wax, the two stones and a few petals into a small cloth bag, and keep it in your bedroom or a shared drawer; if you would rather not keep it, bury it together under a healthy tree or bush on your own property.
chant:
Two lights facing, side by side,
where kindness walks and truths abide.
In patient word and gentle deed,
we give each other what we need.
intention: We choose patience and kindness with each other, freely and together.
timing: Friday (Venus) or Monday (Moon) evening, waxing moon.
bestTime: Any season; good after a stressful period or before a big shared change.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) whenever you step away and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Figure candles burn unevenly and can drip or flare where limbs are thin, so use a large tray with a rim, keep the candles at least 4 inches apart until the final night, and never leave them for a moment. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands after dressing, and never use essential oils undiluted or on broken skin. Keep the herb ring on the plate at least 3 inches from the flame and watch it the whole time, since dried plant material catches fire easily. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, keep a lid or snuffer and water nearby, and smother a wax fire with a lid; never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. This spell is only for two consenting adults in an existing relationship; it is not a substitute for counseling, and anyone who feels unsafe with a partner should reach out to a domestic violence hotline. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, and even diffused or spilled oil can harm them. Lavender is toxic to cats and dogs if eaten, so sweep up the herb ring afterward.

name: Red Pillar Date Night Passion Candle
description: Red is the color of passion, desire and vitality in most modern candle-color systems, and a shared candle lit for romance is a popular folk practice. In this spell an existing couple, both willing, carve one red pillar together, each adding words of desire on their own side, and light it only on date nights over a month. The candle becomes a little ritual of turning toward each other, so passion is fed by attention as well as by flame.
steps: Agree together that you both want this candle and choose your first date night. Cleanse the pillar by wiping it together with a cloth dampened in salt water, each saying, 'Only what is ours.'
Mix the Ginger and Patchouli Essential Oils into the Sweet Almond Oil to make a dressing oil.

Each partner takes one side of the pillar and, carving away from the hand with the toothpick, writes one word of desire, such as 'spark' or 'play', and draws a small heart. Together carve a line around the candle joining the two sides.
Each dresses their own side with a drop or two of oil, stroking upward from the base to the middle only, keeping oil off the wick and the top half inch. Wipe off the excess and wash your hands.
Mix the Damiana and Cinnamon and dust only the bottom inch of the pillar very lightly, then set it on the plate and lay the two stones on either side.
Light the candle together, speak the chant together, then tell each other one memory of when you first felt drawn to each other.
Let it burn through dinner, a dance or a long talk, never longer than three hours, and snuff it together when the evening ends.
howToUse: Light the pillar only on date nights, about once a week for a month or until it is used up, and give each other your full attention while it burns. Each of you carries one stone on the days between. When it is finished, let the wax cool completely, pop the leftover wax from the plate, and keep a small piece wrapped in red cloth in your bedroom drawer; bin the rest respectfully or bury it under a rose bush.
chant:
Flame of red and ember bright,
warm the hearts that meet tonight.
Side by side and hand in hand,
kindle what we both have planned.
intention: We feed the fire between us with attention, play and desire freely given.
timing: Friday (Venus) or Tuesday (Mars) evening, waxing to full moon.
bestTime: Spring or summer, especially around Beltane; or any time you want to rekindle closeness.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) whenever you step away and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Burn a pillar no more than three hours at a time, trimming the wick to 1/4 inch before each lighting, and do not leave it burning if you step away from the room. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands after dressing, and never use essential oils undiluted or on broken skin. Ginger and Patchouli oils are diluted here; do not use this candle oil as a massage oil, and keep Cinnamon dust away from eyes and skin. Rolling a candle in dried herbs is a real fire risk, so use only a light dusting of finely ground herb on the lower part of the candle, never near the wick, and watch it the whole time. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, keep a lid or snuffer and water nearby, and smother a wax fire with a lid; never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. This candle is for an existing couple who both agree to it. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, and even diffused or spilled oil can harm them. Ground Cinnamon can irritate a pet's mouth and lungs.

name: White Pillar Peace for the Home
description: White candles are used across many folk and modern traditions for peace, purity and calm, and keeping a light burning in the main room of a house is an old hearth custom in many cultures. In this spell a white pillar is carved with a house and a dove, dressed with peaceful oil, and lit in the room where the household gathers for short sessions over seven evenings. It invites a softer, calmer atmosphere for everyone who lives there.

ingredients.item: White pillar candle (3 x 4 or 3 x 6 inch)
Peaceful Home Oil (or 3 drops Lavender Essential Oil in 1 tsp Olive Oil)

steps: Open a window and cleanse the candle by wiping it with a cloth dampened in salt water, saying, 'Let only peace be carried here.'
Carving away from your hand with the toothpick, draw a simple house shape on one side of the pillar and a dove or a wavy line for calm water on the other. Beneath them write the word 'peace'.
Dress the candle with a few drops of oil, stroking from the top half inch downward to the base, keeping oil off the wick and the top half inch, then wipe off the excess and wash your hands.

Set the pillar on the plate in the main room. Mix the salt with the Lavender, Chamomile and Basil and sprinkle it in a ring on the plate, at least 3 inches from the candle, and place the Selenite or Quartz in front.
Light the candle and slowly speak the chant three times, imagining soft white light filling the room and drifting into every other room of the house.
Sit quietly for 15 minutes, or invite the household to sit with you and each name one thing that makes home feel safe.
Close by saying, 'Peace stays when the flame goes out,' and snuff the candle.
howToUse: Relight the pillar for 15 to 30 minutes on seven evenings in a row, ideally at the same time, and again any evening the house feels tense. When the candle is finished or you choose to end the spell, let the wax cool completely, then sweep the herb ring and salt into a paper bag and put it in the outside trash bin. Keep a piece of the leftover wax on a high shelf in the main room as a token of household peace, and bin the rest respectfully.
chant:
White light rising, calm and clear,
let only peace be welcome here.
Soft the voice and kind the word,
in every room let love be heard.
intention: I fill my home with a calm, gentle peace that everyone here can feel.
timing: Monday (Moon) or Friday (Venus) evening; any moon phase, especially waxing.
bestTime: Any season; especially after moving, during a stressful time, or after a quarrel.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) whenever you step away and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Choose a spot in the main room where nobody will brush past the candle, and trim the wick to 1/4 inch before each lighting. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands after dressing, and never use essential oils undiluted or on broken skin. Keep the herb ring on the plate at least 3 inches from the flame and watch it the whole time, since dried plant material catches fire easily. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, keep a lid or snuffer and water nearby, and smother a wax fire with a lid; never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, and even diffused or spilled oil can harm them. Lavender, Chamomile and Basil can upset a pet's stomach if eaten, so set the plate up high and clear the herb ring when you finish.

name: Open Heart Rose Quartz Taper
description: Rose Quartz is one of the best-known love stones in modern crystal practice, linked with an open, gentle heart, and pink candles are a contemporary favorite for drawing love in general. This spell does not name or seek any particular person: a pink taper is carved with an open heart, dressed with attraction oil, and ringed with Rose Quartz to soften old guarding and make you ready to give and receive love freely. It is as much about opening yourself as about calling love in.

ingredients.item: Pink taper candle (8 or 10 inch, dripless if possible)
Sturdy taper holder on a heatproof plate
Attraction Oil (or 2 drops Rose Essential Oil and 1 drop Ylang Ylang Essential Oil in 1 tsp Sweet Almond Oil)
Salt water in a small bowl

steps: Cleanse the taper by dipping your fingers in the salt water and drawing them down the candle three times, then pat it dry.
Carving away from your hand with the toothpick, draw a heart in the middle of the taper with a small gap at the top, an open heart, and write 'open' beneath it.

Dress the candle with a few drops of oil, stroking from the bottom of the candle upward to the heart to draw love toward you, keeping oil off the wick and the top half inch. Wipe off the excess and wash your hands.

Fix the taper upright in its holder on the plate. Set the five Rose Quartz stones in a ring around the holder, and sprinkle the Rose and Hibiscus in a wider ring on the plate, at least 3 inches from the flame.
Light the taper, place your hand over your heart and speak the chant three times.
For 15 minutes, breathe slowly and imagine a door in your chest opening; say aloud one old hurt you are ready to stop guarding and one quality of love you are ready to welcome.
Snuff the candle, saying, 'My heart is open; love may enter freely.'
howToUse: Relight the taper for 15 minutes each evening until it reaches the bottom inch, then snuff it for the last time. Carry one Rose Quartz with you and keep the rest by your bed. Once the wax is completely cool, bury the leftover wax stub and the petals under a rose bush or in a flower bed you are allowed to dig, as a seed for new love; if you cannot bury it, wrap it in pink cloth and keep it. Then say yes to new people and new places, since the spell opens you, and you still need to walk out the door.
chant:
Rose of stone and rose of flame,
open what old fears made tame.
Love that's free and love that's true,
my heart is open; come through.
intention: I open my heart and welcome a kind love that comes to me freely.
timing: Friday (Venus) evening during the waxing moon.
bestTime: Spring, especially near Beltane, or any time you feel ready for love.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) whenever you step away and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Tapers can lean or drip, so make sure the candle is firmly fixed upright, keep it away from drafts, and snuff it when it reaches the last inch so the holder does not overheat. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands after dressing, and never use essential oils undiluted or on broken skin. Keep the herb ring on the plate at least 3 inches from the flame and watch it the whole time, since dried plant material catches fire easily. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, keep a lid or snuffer and water nearby, and smother a wax fire with a lid; never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. Keep the small stones away from young children, who could choke on them. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, and even diffused or spilled oil can harm them. Keep the stones and herbs where pets cannot swallow them.

name: Circle of Friends Tealight Spell
description: Yellow is linked with friendship, warmth and cheerful company in many modern candle-color systems, and a circle is an old symbol of belonging. In this spell a ring of yellow tealights stands for you and your friends, with one extra light for friends still to come, and each light is carved with an initial and dressed underneath so the oil stays well away from the flame. It blesses the friendships you have and opens a place for new ones.

ingredients.item: Yellow tealight candles in metal cups (4 to 5 hour)
ingredients.amount: 1 for you, 1 for each close friend, and 1 extra

ingredients.item: Salt water and a soft cloth

steps: Cleanse the tealights by wiping each metal cup and the top of the wax with a cloth dampened in salt water, then let them dry.

Carving away from your hand with the toothpick, scratch an initial into the top of each tealight, well clear of the wick: your own, one for each friend, and a small star on the extra light for friends yet to come.

Mix the Sweet Orange Essential Oil into the Sweet Almond Oil to make the dressing oil. To dress each candle safely, gently push each tealight out of its cup, dab a single drop of oil on the underside of the wax, wipe off any excess, and press it back into the cup so no oil sits on top. Wash your hands.

Set the Citrine or Amazonite in the center of the tray and arrange the tealights in a circle around it, at least 3 inches apart so they do not heat each other. Sprinkle the Lemon Balm and Chamomile in a thin outer ring on the tray, 3 inches from the nearest flame.
Light your own tealight first, then use a long match or wooden spill to light each friend's candle, saying each friend's name and one thing you love about them.
Light the star candle last and speak the chant, then sit with the circle for 20 minutes, sending each friend a kind message if you like.
Close by saying, 'Bound in kindness, free in choice,' and snuff each tealight in the order you lit them.
howToUse: Relight the circle once a week for a month, or on a night when you gather with friends, until the tealights burn down. Carry the stone when you meet friends or go somewhere you hope to make new ones. Once the leftover wax is completely cool, pop each disk out of its cup, keep your own and the star disk together in a small yellow bag, and give the others back to the earth by burying them or binning them respectfully; recycle the empty metal cups.
chant:
Light by light, a ring of cheer,
friends I love and friends drawn near.
Laughing, loyal, kind and true,
there's a place in here for you.
intention: I bless the friends who love me and make room for good new friends.
timing: Sunday (Sun) or Wednesday (Mercury) evening, waxing moon.
bestTime: Spring or summer; also before a move, a new school year or a new job.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) whenever you step away and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Keep tealights in their metal cups and at least 3 inches apart, since grouped tealights can heat each other until the wax pools and flares; never set them directly on wood or plastic, and let the cups cool before touching them. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands after dressing, and never use essential oils undiluted or on broken skin. Here the single drop of oil goes only on the underside of each tealight. Sweet Orange oil can irritate sensitive skin. Keep the herb ring on the plate at least 3 inches from the flame and watch it the whole time, since dried plant material catches fire easily. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, keep a lid or snuffer and water nearby, and smother a wax fire with a lid; never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, and even diffused or spilled oil can harm them. Citrus oils are especially risky for cats, and Chamomile can upset pets if eaten.

name: Honeyed Reconciliation Seven-Day Candle
description: Sweetening work belongs to the African American folk tradition of hoodoo, where honey jars and sugar have long been used to make situations and relationships sweeter; many rootworkers taste the honey while saying 'as this honey is sweet to me...'. This candle spell borrows that idea respectfully and does not try to force anyone's feelings. A seven-day glass-jar candle is lit for a quarrel or estrangement you sincerely want to mend, and each night you taste a little honey, sweeten your own words, and ask that both sides be open to an honest, kind conversation if that is right for you both.

ingredients.item: Pink or white glass-jar 7-day candle (about 8 inches)
Reconciliation Oil (or 3 drops Rose Essential Oil in 1 tsp Sweet Almond Oil)
Honey in a small dish, with a clean spoon

steps: Cleanse the outside of the glass jar with a cloth dampened in salt water, then wipe it dry.

On the paper, write a petition for the situation, not for control: for example, 'May there be peace between me and my sister, may we both be willing to listen, and may this be sweetened only if it is right for us both.' Fold it toward you three times and slide it beneath the heatproof plate, never under the hot glass itself.
With the toothpick, carving away from your hand, draw a heart and two joined circles into the top surface of the wax, around but not touching the wick.

Dress the top of the wax with three drops of oil near the rim, away from the wick, and wipe up any pooled oil with a tissue. Add only a tiny pinch of crumbled Lavender at the outer edge, well away from the wick. Wash your hands.
Set the jar on the plate on a heatproof surface, away from windows and drafts, with the stone in front and the dish of honey beside it.
Take a small spoonful of honey and say, 'As this honey is sweet to me, so let my words be sweet and true, and may our hearts be open.' Then light the candle and speak the chant.
Sit for 15 to 30 minutes thinking of what you honestly want to say and what you are sorry for, then snuff the candle with a lid or snuffer.
howToUse: Relight the candle each evening for seven nights, beginning each session with a taste of honey from a clean spoon and the same words. Do not let it burn while you are out or asleep, and stop and remove the candle when only half an inch of wax is left in the jar. By the last night, take a real step: send a kind message, apologize, or simply let the other person know the door is open, and respect their answer either way. Once the jar is completely cool, scoop out the leftover wax and bury it with the petition under a flowering plant or near your front door; wash and recycle the glass. Pour the used honey dish into the compost.
chant:
Honey on my tongue, my words made kind,
open heart and open mind.
If it's right, let the bridge be mended,
let the bitter days be ended.
intention: I sweeten my own words and open the door to peace, if it is right for us both.
timing: Friday (Venus) or Monday (Moon), beginning on a waxing moon.
bestTime: Any season; especially before holidays or family gatherings.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) whenever you step away and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Glass-jar candles can crack when hot, so keep this one on a heatproof surface, never in a window, and never let it burn dry. Stop burning when half an inch of wax remains. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands after dressing, and never use essential oils undiluted or on broken skin. Keep the oil and the tiny pinch of herb at the outer edge of the wax, away from the wick, and watch the flame the whole time. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, keep a lid or snuffer and water nearby, and smother a wax fire with a lid; never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. This spell asks for openness on both sides and never for anyone to be forced back; if the relationship was abusive, do not use it to reopen contact. Do not give honey to babies under one year old because of the risk of infant botulism. Edible part: a small taste of plain honey from a clean spoon each night; nothing else in the spell is eaten or drunk.
interactions: No drug interactions are expected from a small taste of honey, but people managing diabetes should count it as sugar.
pets: Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, and even diffused or spilled oil can harm them. Keep honey away from pets.

name: Family Circle Unity Pillar
description: Hearth fires and family candles have been gathering points in homes across many cultures, and in modern candle magic brown and green are often used for home, steadiness and growth. In this spell every member of the household, children included with an adult's help, carves their own mark into one large pillar, so the whole family is held in a single flame. It is lit at a weekly family gathering to strengthen belonging, patience and loyalty among everyone who lives together.

ingredients.item: Brown or green pillar candle (3 x 6 inch or larger)
Blessing Oil (or 3 drops Sweet Orange Essential Oil in 1 tsp Olive Oil)
Family photo or a drawing of your home
Toothpick, pin or blunt pencil for each carver
Salt water and a soft cloth

steps: Gather the household and cleanse the pillar by passing it from hand to hand, each person wiping it once with the salt water cloth and saying, 'Only love here.'

Each person carves their initial or a small symbol into the side of the candle, carving away from the hand; an adult guides young children's hands or carves the mark for them. Carve one circle around the middle of the candle that touches every mark.
An adult dresses the candle with a few drops of oil, stroking from the middle down to the base, keeping oil off the wick and the top half inch, then wipes off the excess. Everyone washes their hands.

Set the pillar on the plate in the middle of the table, with the photo propped at least 12 inches away. Lay the Bay Laurel leaves in a ring on the plate and sprinkle the Rosemary and Basil around them, all at least 3 inches from the flame.
An adult lights the candle while everyone speaks the chant together.
Go around the circle: each person names one thing they are grateful for in another family member, and one way they will help the family this week.
Share a meal, game or story by candlelight, then an adult snuffs the candle while everyone says, 'Together.'
howToUse: Light the family pillar at the same weekly gathering, such as Sunday dinner, until it is used up, adding the gratitude round each time. When a family member is away, light it for a few minutes and say their name. When it is finished, let the wax cool completely, break off one piece of the leftover wax for each person to keep in a pocket or treasure box, and bury the rest with the Bay leaves under a tree or bush near your home, or bin it respectfully if you cannot dig.
chant:
One flame for all beneath this roof,
our love the wall, our trust the proof.
Through calm and storm, through near and far,
together is the way we are.
intention: Our family is held together in patience, gratitude and love.
timing: Sunday (Sun) evening, waxing or full moon.
bestTime: Any season; especially at the new year, after a move, or when a new member joins the family.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) whenever you step away and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Children may carve and speak but an adult should do all lighting and snuffing, and nobody should reach across the flame; place the candle where no one will bump the table. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool.
