Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands after dressing, and never use essential oils undiluted or on broken skin. Keep the herb ring on the plate at least 3 inches from the flame and watch it the whole time, since dried plant material catches fire easily. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, keep a lid or snuffer and water nearby, and smother a wax fire with a lid; never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, and even diffused or spilled oil can harm them. Bay Laurel is toxic to cats, dogs and horses if eaten, so keep the plate up high and clear the leaves away afterward.

name: Seven-Notch Breakup Healing Candle
description: Marking a candle into sections and burning one section a night is a common technique in American folk candle magic, used to pace a working over several days. In this spell a white taper is notched into seven parts, one for each night of the waning moon, and each night you burn one section and name one thing you are releasing from a relationship that has ended. It does not touch your former partner at all; it is about grieving, letting go and coming back to yourself.

ingredients.item: Sturdy taper holder on a heatproof plate
Healing Oil (or 2 drops Lavender Essential Oil and 1 drop Rosemary Essential Oil in 1 tsp Sweet Almond Oil)

steps: Cleanse the taper by wiping it with a cloth dampened in salt water and saying, 'I begin again.'
Using the ruler, mark the taper into seven equal sections and, carving away from your hand with the pin, scratch a line around the candle at each mark. Leave the bottom inch unmarked.

Dress the candle with a few drops of oil, stroking from the top half inch downward to the base to send the old ties away from you, keeping oil off the wick and the top half inch. Wipe off the excess and wash your hands.
Fix the taper upright in its holder. Sprinkle the Lemon Balm, Rose and Rosemary in a ring on the plate, at least 3 inches from the flame, and set the stone in front.
Light the candle and speak the chant. Write one thing you are releasing tonight, such as 'waiting for their text' or 'blaming myself', and one thing you are reclaiming, such as 'my Sunday mornings'.
Hold the stone and let any feelings come while the first section burns down; this usually takes 20 to 40 minutes. Stay with the candle the whole time.
When the flame reaches the first notch, read your two lines aloud, then snuff the candle, saying, 'One night lighter.'
howToUse: Burn one section on each of seven nights in a row, ideally starting near the full moon so you finish during the waning moon, and stop for the last time at the unmarked bottom inch. Keep the journal pages. When the seven nights are done and the wax is completely cool, take the leftover wax stub and the herbs from the plate and bury them away from your home, at a park edge or under a tree you are allowed to dig near, or put them in a trash bin off your property, and walk away without looking back. Carry the stone for another month. If grief stays heavy, talk to a trusted friend or a counselor; candles are a companion to support, not a replacement for it.
chant:
Notch by notch the old ties burn,
night by night my strength returns.
What was ours I now release;
what is mine comes home in peace.
intention: I release what has ended and come home to myself, one night at a time.
timing: Begin just after the full moon and finish in the waning moon; Saturday (Saturn) or Monday (Moon).
bestTime: Any season, whenever a relationship has ended; autumn suits letting go.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) whenever you step away and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Tapers can lean or drip, so fix the candle firmly upright, keep it out of drafts, and stop at the unmarked bottom inch so the holder does not overheat. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands after dressing, and never use essential oils undiluted or on broken skin. Keep the herb ring on the plate at least 3 inches from the flame and watch it the whole time, since dried plant material catches fire easily. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, keep a lid or snuffer and water nearby, and smother a wax fire with a lid; never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. If you have thoughts of harming yourself, contact a crisis line such as 988 in the US right away. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, and even diffused or spilled oil can harm them. Keep the herbs and stone where pets cannot eat or chew them.

name: Blue Jar Candle for an Anxious Mind
description: Pale blue is used in many modern candle-color systems for calm, peace and soothing, and steady flame-gazing is a simple focusing practice found in several meditation traditions. In this spell a light-blue glass-jar candle is dressed with calming oil and lit for a short evening sitting, paired with slow breathing timed to the flame. It is a gentle nightly ritual to help a racing mind settle; it supports, but does not replace, care from a doctor or therapist.

ingredients.item: Jojoba Oil or Sweet Almond Oil

steps: Cleanse the outside of the jar with a cloth dampened in salt water, then wipe it dry.
With the skewer, carving away from your hand, draw a gentle wave and the word 'calm' into the top surface of the wax, around but not touching the wick.

Mix the Lavender and Roman Chamomile Essential Oils into the carrier oil. Dress the top of the wax with two or three drops near the rim, away from the wick, wipe up any pooling, and add a tiny pinch of crumbled Chamomile at the outer edge. Wash your hands.
Set the jar on the plate on a table or desk, never in a window or near curtains, with the stone in front of it.
Light the candle, hold the stone, and speak the chant once slowly.
Watch the flame and breathe: in for a count of four, hold for four, out for six. Each time you breathe out, picture one worry floating into the blue light. Continue for 10 to 15 minutes.
Close by naming one small, kind thing you will do for yourself before bed, then snuff the candle with its lid or a snuffer.
howToUse: Light the candle for 10 to 15 minutes each evening, or whenever worry spikes, until it is used up; stop when half an inch of wax remains in the jar. Keep the stone in your pocket or under your pillow and hold it while repeating the breathing when you cannot light the candle. Once the jar is fully cool, scoop out the leftover wax, wrap it in paper and put it in the trash, saying, 'I let this worry go'; wash and recycle the glass. If anxiety is affecting your sleep, work or relationships, please talk to a health professional.
chant:
Blue as water, still and deep,
quiet the thoughts that will not sleep.
Breath by breath and flame by flame,
my mind grows calm and clear again.
intention: I breathe slowly, let my thoughts settle, and allow myself to feel calm.
timing: Monday (Moon) evening; any moon phase, especially the waning moon to ease worry.
bestTime: Any season; especially busy or stressful times of year.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) whenever you step away and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Glass-jar candles can crack when hot, so keep this one on a heatproof surface, never in a window, and never let it burn dry. Stop burning when half an inch of wax remains, and never fall asleep with it lit; snuff it before you get into bed. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands after dressing, and never use essential oils undiluted or on broken skin. Keep the tiny pinch of herb at the outer edge of the wax, away from the wick, and watch the flame the whole time. People allergic to ragweed or daisies may react to Chamomile. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, keep a lid or snuffer and water nearby, and smother a wax fire with a lid; never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. This ritual is not a treatment for anxiety disorders; if you have thoughts of harming yourself, contact a crisis line such as 988 in the US. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, and even diffused or spilled oil can harm them. Lavender and Chamomile are toxic to pets if eaten.

name: Braided Cord and Two Taper Bond Spell
description: Knotted and braided cords appear in many European folk charms, and in modern handfasting, cords are wrapped around joined hands to show a shared promise. In this spell two people who both want a stronger bond, whether partners, close friends or family, each light a taper and braid three strands into one cord between them: one for each person and one for what you share. The cord is never tied to the candles; it is braided and knotted beside them and kept as a token afterward.

ingredients.item: Taper candles (8 or 10 inch) in pink, red or white, each person choosing their own color
Sturdy taper holders on a heatproof tray
Cotton or wool cords or embroidery threads, about 18 inches each, in three colors
Blessing Oil (or 3 drops Rose Geranium Essential Oil in 1 tsp Sweet Almond Oil)

steps: Agree together that you both want this bond strengthened and say what kind of bond it is, such as 'loving partners' or 'sisters who stay close'. Cleanse both tapers by wiping them with a cloth dampened in salt water.
Each person carves their own first name down their own taper, carving away from the hand with the toothpick, then carves a small circle at the base for the circle you share.
Each person dresses their own taper with a drop or two of oil, stroking from the base up to the middle, keeping oil off the wick and the top half inch. Wipe off the excess and wash your hands.

Fix the tapers upright in their holders on the tray, about 12 inches apart. Sprinkle the Rose and Vervain in a line on the tray between them, at least 3 inches from each flame, and place a stone in front of each candle.
Each lights the other's candle and you speak the chant together. Then, sitting well back from the flames, knot the three cords together at one end.

One person holds the knot while the other braids, or take turns, saying one promise for every few crossings, such as 'I'll call when it's hard' or 'I'll listen first'. Knot the other end when the braid is done.
Lay the braided cord on the table in front of the tray, never on it or near the flames, let the candles burn 10 more minutes while you talk, then snuff them together.
howToUse: Relight the tapers together for 15 minutes on two more evenings, holding the braided cord between you while you speak the chant, then let them burn on a last session until the final inch and snuff them. Each person keeps one stone. Keep the cord in a box or hang it in a shared space; if you live apart, cut it in half after snuffing, knot the cut ends, and each keep one half. Once the leftover wax is completely cool, press the two stubs together into one lump and keep it with the cord, or bury it together under a tree you both love.
chant:
Three strands crossing, one cord true,
my part, your part, and what we grew.
Braided strong and knotted tight,
held by choice and held by light.
intention: We freely choose to strengthen the bond we share, with care and honesty.
timing: Friday (Venus) or Thursday (Jupiter) evening, waxing moon.
bestTime: Any season; lovely near an anniversary, a reunion, or before a time apart.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; snuff it (do not blow it out) whenever you step away and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Never tie cord, thread or ribbon to a candle or let it hang near a flame; braid well back from the tray and keep the finished cord off it. Tapers can lean or drip, so fix them firmly and snuff them at the last inch. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands after dressing, and never use essential oils undiluted or on broken skin. Keep the herb ring on the plate at least 3 inches from the flame and watch it the whole time, since dried plant material catches fire easily. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, keep a lid or snuffer and water nearby, and smother a wax fire with a lid; never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let wax cool completely before handling it, and never pour hot wax down a drain. This spell is only for people who both agree to it. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, and even diffused or spilled oil can harm them. Keep cords and threads away from pets, especially cats, since swallowed string can cause serious intestinal blockage.

name: Black Pillar Negativity-Absorbing Candle
description: In many modern Wiccan and folk practices, black is the color that absorbs, the way dark cloth soaks up heat. A black candle is lit to draw heaviness, tension and stray ill will out of a room or a person and burn it away as harmless smoke and light. This version uses a pillar set in a dish of salt, so the salt catches what the flame releases.

ingredients.item: Black pillar candle, about 3 inches wide and 4-6 inches tall
Heatproof plate or shallow ceramic dish
Cast Off Evil Oil (or Olive Oil with 2 drops Black Pepper Essential Oil)
Toothpick or blunt pin for carving

steps: Cleanse the black pillar by wiping it with a cloth dampened in salt water, then dry it well and hold it while you name the heaviness you want it to take in.
Using a toothpick and carving away from your hand, carve a downward spiral from the top of the candle toward the base, picturing negativity being drawn down and out.
Dress the candle with a few drops of Cast Off Evil Oil, stroking from top to bottom, keeping oil off the wick and the top half inch; wipe off any excess and wash your hands.
Pour the salt onto the heatproof plate, set the pillar firmly in the center, and dust the finely ground Rosemary onto the salt in a ring around the base, not on the candle.
Set the Black Tourmaline on the salt at the front of the plate, at least 2 inches from the flame.
Light the candle and say the chant three times, then sit quietly and imagine the room's heaviness flowing into the dark flame and rising away as light.
Let it burn for one hour or more while you stay with it, then close by snuffing the flame and saying, 'Taken in, burned clean, done.' Repeat on following nights until the pillar is used up.
howToUse: Burn it in sessions on consecutive nights, always snuffing it when you leave the room. When it is finished, let everything cool completely, then wrap the leftover wax and the salt together in paper and put them in an outdoor trash bin away from your home, since they hold what was absorbed. Rinse the Black Tourmaline under running water and keep it near your door.
chant:
Black of night and dark of stone,
draw the weight from hearth and home.
What is heavy, take it in;
burn it clean, let peace begin.
intention: I let this flame draw every heavy and unwanted energy out of my space and burn it clean.
timing: Saturday, during a waning moon; any time a room feels heavy after conflict or illness.
bestTime: Any season; especially late autumn and winter.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; if you must stop, snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray, at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands afterward and never use oils on broken skin. Dried herbs near a flame are a real fire risk: keep them as a light dusting on the lower part only or in a ring on the plate, watch the candle the whole time, and keep a snuffer or lid and a cup of water nearby. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, never put glitter, paper or plastic on the candle, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire (smother it with a lid instead). Let wax cool completely before handling and never pour hot wax down a drain. Black Pepper Essential Oil can irritate skin, so dilute it in carrier oil and keep it away from eyes. Salt can damage wood finishes, so keep it on the plate. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Salt is harmful to pets if licked up in quantity (vomiting, tremors, seizures), so keep the plate out of reach and bin the salt afterward. Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, so keep them out of the room while the candle burns and until it has aired out.

name: Double-Action Reversing Candle
description: In hoodoo and related folk practice, a 'double action' or reversing candle (often red on the outside with a black core, or half black and half red) is burned to turn back harm that was sent your way. Practitioners are careful to describe this as returning what was sent, not adding to it. This working sends harm back to its source with the explicit condition that it arrives harmlessly, as a lesson rather than a wound.

ingredients.item: Black-and-red double-action taper candle, about 9-10 inches (or a red taper with black wax dripped at its base)
Sturdy taper holder on a heatproof tray
Small mirror, glass side up, about 4-6 inches across, or a square of foil shiny side up

steps: Cleanse the taper by passing it slowly over a bowl of salt water and wiping it dry, saying, 'Only what was sent, and nothing more.'
Carve your name near the base of the candle and, above it, an arrow pointing upward and away from your name, carving away from your hand.
Dress the taper with Uncrossing Oil, stroking from the middle out toward each end, keeping oil off the wick and the top half inch; wipe off the excess and wash your hands.
Dust a very light pinch of finely ground Hyssop onto the lower third of the taper only, then lay the mirror on the tray and stand the holder on top of it so the candle's light reflects up and out.
Tuck the Bay Laurel leaf flat under the edge of the mirror, well away from the flame.
Light the candle and speak the chant, stating aloud that whatever returns must do so harmlessly and teach rather than wound.
Watch the candle for at least one hour, then close by snuffing it and saying, 'Returned in peace; I am clear.' Relight it on following days until it is gone.
howToUse: Burn the taper over one to three sessions, snuffing it between them. When it is finished and fully cool, scrape up the leftover wax with the Bay Laurel leaf, wrap them in paper, and put them in a trash bin at a crossroads or anywhere away from your home, without looking back. Wipe the mirror with salt water before using it for anything else.
chant:
What was sent comes home again,
soft as rain and free of pain.
No harm to them, no harm to me;
returned in peace, so mote it be.
intention: I return any harm sent to me back to its source, harmlessly and in peace.
timing: Saturday or Tuesday, during a waning moon.
bestTime: Any season, when you sense ill will directed at you.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; if you must stop, snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray, at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Tapers can drip and tip, so make sure the holder grips the candle snugly and is stable on the mirror; use a mirror with smooth or taped edges and keep it from overheating by setting the holder base, not the flame, over it. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands afterward and never use oils on broken skin. Dried herbs near a flame are a real fire risk: keep them as a light dusting on the lower part only or in a ring on the plate, watch the candle the whole time, and keep a snuffer or lid and a cup of water nearby. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, never put glitter, paper or plastic on the candle, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire (smother it with a lid instead). Let wax cool completely before handling and never pour hot wax down a drain. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, so keep them out of the room while the candle burns and until it has aired out. Bay Laurel leaves can upset a pet's stomach if chewed.

name: White Candle Salt Ring Protection
description: White candles are used in many traditions for general protection and blessing, and salt has long marked boundaries that harm should not cross. Here a small salt ring is poured on a tray around a single white candle, making a miniature warded space that stands for your home or yourself. It is a compact protection working for apartments, offices and anyone who cannot pour a full salt circle on the floor.

ingredients.item: White taper or white chime candle, 4-10 inches
Angelica root, dried and finely ground (or Rosemary)

steps: Cleanse the candle by holding it in both hands and breathing out slowly over it three times, then wiping it with a clean cloth.
Carve a simple shield or a circle with a dot in its center into the side of the candle, carving away from your hand, and carve your initials beneath it.
Dress the candle with Fiery Wall of Protection Oil from base to middle only, keeping oil off the wick and the top half inch; wipe off the excess and wash your hands.
Set the candle in its holder in the middle of the tray, then pour an unbroken ring of salt around it about 3 inches from the base, starting in the east and moving clockwise.
Sprinkle the ground Angelica along the salt ring, and set one Clear Quartz at each of the four directions on the ring.
Light the candle and say the chant, picturing the salt ring rising into a bright wall around you and everything you love.
Stay with the flame for 20 minutes or longer, then close by snuffing it and saying, 'The ring holds.' Leave the salt ring in place on the tray until the candle is finished.
howToUse: Relight the candle in short, attended sessions until it is used up, keeping the ring unbroken between sessions. When done and fully cool, bury the leftover wax at the edge of your property or under a houseplant's outer pot (not in the soil), or keep a small piece in a pouch by your door as a token of the ward. Pour the salt away down an outdoor drain with running water, not on soil, and cleanse the quartz before reusing it.
chant:
White of light and salt of sea,
ring of guard surrounding me.
No harm may cross, no ill may stay;
what's mine is kept by night and day.
intention: I surround myself and my home with a wall of protection no harm can cross.
timing: Sunday or Saturday, at any moon phase; especially full moon.
bestTime: Any season; good when moving into a new home or office.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; if you must stop, snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray, at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Fiery Wall of Protection Oil commonly contains cinnamon or other warming oils that can irritate skin; use only a few drops and wash your hands right after. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands afterward and never use oils on broken skin. Dried herbs near a flame are a real fire risk: keep them as a light dusting on the lower part only or in a ring on the plate, watch the candle the whole time, and keep a snuffer or lid and a cup of water nearby. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, never put glitter, paper or plastic on the candle, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire (smother it with a lid instead). Let wax cool completely before handling and never pour hot wax down a drain. Keep salt off wood, plants and soil. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep the tray out of reach; salt eaten by dogs or cats can cause vomiting, tremors and seizures, and small quartz pieces are a choking hazard. Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, so keep them out of the room while the candle burns and until it has aired out.

name: Purple Psychic Sight Candle
description: Purple is linked with intuition and spiritual sight in modern Western color magic, and many readers light a candle before laying out cards, scrying or using a pendulum. This short working uses a purple chime candle, which burns in about two hours, to mark the start and end of a divination session and settle the mind. It does not replace practice or common sense; it helps you shift into a focused, receptive state.

ingredients.item: Chime candle holder on a heatproof plate
Psychic Vision Oil (or 1 tsp Sweet Almond Oil with 2 drops Lavender Essential Oil)
Your tarot deck, pendulum or scrying bowl

steps: Cleanse the candle and your tools by setting them on a windowsill in moonlight for a few minutes, or by ringing a bell over them three times.
Carve an open eye, or a crescent moon with a dot above it, into the candle, carving away from your hand.
Dress the candle with Psychic Vision Oil, stroking upward from base toward the middle to draw sight upward, keeping oil off the wick and the top half inch; wipe off the excess and wash your hands.
Set the candle in its holder on the plate and sprinkle the Mugwort in a small ring on the plate around the base, not on the candle.
Hold the Amethyst to your forehead for a few breaths, then set it beside your deck or pendulum.
Light the candle, say the chant, and begin your reading while the candle burns beside you.
When the reading is finished, thank your guides, snuff the flame, and touch the deck or pendulum to the cool base of the candle to close the session.
howToUse: Use the candle across one or two reading sessions, snuffing it in between. When it has burned down and cooled, keep a small piece of the leftover purple wax wrapped with your deck or pendulum as a reminder of the session, and put the rest in the trash. Write down the reading and any impressions afterward.
chant:
Violet flame and lifted veil,
show me truth in clear detail.
Sight to see and sense to know;
what is hidden, gently show.
intention: I open my inner sight to see clearly and truthfully during this reading.
timing: Monday, evening or night; full or waxing moon.
bestTime: Any season; especially autumn around Samhain.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; if you must stop, snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray, at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands afterward and never use oils on broken skin. Dried herbs near a flame are a real fire risk: keep them as a light dusting on the lower part only or in a ring on the plate, watch the candle the whole time, and keep a snuffer or lid and a cup of water nearby. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, never put glitter, paper or plastic on the candle, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire (smother it with a lid instead). Let wax cool completely before handling and never pour hot wax down a drain. Avoid Mugwort if you are pregnant, trying to conceive or breastfeeding, and if you are allergic to ragweed, daisies or related plants. If using Sweet Almond Oil, skip it with nut allergies and use Jojoba Oil instead. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, so keep them out of the room while the candle burns and until it has aired out.

name: Silver Full Moon Taper Blessing
description: Silver is the color of the moon in much of modern Wicca and Western ceremonial magic, and the full moon is widely treated as the peak time for blessing, gratitude and charging tools. This working uses a silver taper set in a bowl of water so the flame's reflection 'catches' the moon on the altar. It is a monthly blessing for yourself, your tools and your home.

ingredients.item: Silver taper candle, about 10 inches (or a white taper)
Wide, heatproof bowl or deep tray

ingredients.amount: enough to fill the bowl 1 inch deep

ingredients.item: Jasmine or White Rose petals, dried

steps: Cleanse the taper by holding it up to the moon (through a window is fine) and asking that it be made clean and bright.
Carve a full circle near the top of the candle, a crescent on each side of it, and the word 'Bless' along the length, carving away from your hand.
Dress the taper with Full Moon Oil from the middle outward to each end, keeping oil off the wick and the top half inch; wipe off the excess and wash your hands.
Set the holder in the center of the bowl, pour in water to about 1 inch deep around the holder base (not above it), and float the petals on the water.
Place the Moonstone or Selenite beside the bowl, not in the water, since Selenite dissolves when wet.
Light the taper, look at its reflection on the water, and say the chant, then name aloud three things you are grateful for this month.
After at least 30 minutes, close by snuffing the flame and saying, 'Full and bright, blessed and right.' Relight it on following full-moon nights or the next two evenings until it is finished.
howToUse: Burn the taper in attended sessions over the full moon and the two nights after. Pour the water onto the earth (not down a drain if it has wax in it; skim the wax off first). When the candle is done and cool, keep the leftover silver wax in a small dish on your altar and add each month's remnant, then melt them together into a new small candle at the year's end or bury them under a tree.
chant:
Silver lady, round and bright,
bless this home and bless this night.
What I hold and what I keep,
bathe in light from height to deep.
intention: I welcome the full moon's blessing on myself, my tools and my home.
timing: The night of the full moon or the two nights after; Monday is especially fitting.
bestTime: Every full moon of the year; harvest moon in September or October for gratitude.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; if you must stop, snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray, at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Keep the water level below the top of the holder so the candle stays stable and dry, and never use the water as a substitute for a heatproof surface. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands afterward and never use oils on broken skin. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, never put glitter, paper or plastic on the candle, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire (smother it with a lid instead). Let wax cool completely before handling and never pour hot wax down a drain. Petals belong on the water only, never on the candle. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, so keep them out of the room while the candle burns and until it has aired out. Keep pets from drinking the oily bowl water.

name: New Moon Seed Tealight
description: The new moon is traditionally the time to begin, when the sky is dark and anything planted can grow along with the waxing light. In this simple working, one intention is carved into a tealight that sits beside a single seed, and the seed is planted once the candle has burned. It is quick, small and suited to beginners or to a busy month.

ingredients.item: White or green tealight candle in its metal cup
New Moon Oil (or 1 tsp Olive Oil with 1 drop Sweet Orange Essential Oil)
Seed: a sunflower, bean or basil seed

steps: Cleanse the tealight by lifting it out of its cup, wiping it with a clean cloth, and holding it at your heart while you breathe slowly three times.
With a toothpick, carve one key word for your intention into the flat top surface of the wax, around the wick, carving away from your hand and keeping marks shallow.
Dress the tealight by rubbing one or two drops of New Moon Oil onto the sides of the wax only, well away from the wick, then place it back in its metal cup and wash your hands.
Set the tealight on the saucer, sprinkle the tiny pinch of Basil on the saucer near the cup, and put the seed beside it.
Light the tealight, hold the seed in your palm, and say the chant while picturing your intention already growing.
Let the tealight burn while you stay nearby, for up to 4 hours, or snuff it and relight it on the next waxing nights.
Close by planting the seed in the pot, watering it, and saying, 'As this grows, so grows my wish.'
howToUse: Tend the seedling through the waxing moon as a living reminder of your intention. When the tealight is spent and cool, pop the little disc of leftover wax out of the metal cup and press it into the soil surface beside the pot's rim for one moon cycle, then lift it out and bin it; recycle the aluminum cup.
chant:
Dark moon, new moon, seed and flame,
I plant my wish and speak its name.
As light returns and grows anew,
let what I sow come growing through.
intention: I plant this intention at the new moon and let it grow with the returning light.
timing: The night of the new moon or within a day after; Sunday or Monday.
bestTime: Any month; spring new moons are especially fitting.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; if you must stop, snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray, at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Tealights get hot right through the metal cup, so always set them on a saucer and never on a bare surface or plastic. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands afterward and never use oils on broken skin. Dried herbs near a flame are a real fire risk: keep them as a light dusting on the lower part only or in a ring on the plate, watch the candle the whole time, and keep a snuffer or lid and a cup of water nearby. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, never put glitter, paper or plastic on the candle, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire (smother it with a lid instead). Let wax cool completely before handling and never pour hot wax down a drain. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, so keep them out of the room while the candle burns and until it has aired out. Choose a seed that is safe if a pet digs it up; avoid toxic plants if pets share the room.

name: Blue Seven-Day Healing Support Candle
description: Blue is associated with calm and healing in many modern color-magic systems, and seven-day glass-jar candles are a staple of hoodoo and Catholic folk devotion for steady, ongoing prayer. This working keeps a gentle flame of support burning in attended sessions through a week of treatment or recovery. It is meant to support, and never to replace, care from doctors, nurses and other medical professionals.

ingredients.item: Heatproof plate or tile, larger than the jar base
Blue Lace Agate or Clear Quartz
Paper and pen for the name and well-wishes

steps: Cleanse the jar by wiping the outside glass with a cloth dampened in salt water, then dry it fully.
With a toothpick, carve the first name of the person being supported (yourself or someone who has agreed) and a small heart into the top surface of the wax, carving away from your hand.
Dress the candle: make three small holes in the top wax with the toothpick, at least 1 inch from the wick, and add one drop of Healing Oil to each; wipe up any oil on the glass and wash your hands.
Place a pinch of crumbled Calendula and a few Lavender buds into those same holes only, well away from the wick, then set the jar on the heatproof plate.
Write the name and your well-wishes on the slip of paper and tuck it under the plate, not under the jar or near the flame, with the stone on top of the paper.
Light the candle and say the chant, then picture the person resting comfortably and following their care plan with strength.
Close each session by snuffing the flame and saying, 'Rest and mend, the light remains.' Relight it once or twice each day for seven days or until it finishes.
howToUse: Burn the candle in attended sessions of an hour or more over about a week, keeping up any medical appointments and treatments as directed. Stop before the wax burns completely dry to protect the glass. Once cool, scoop out any leftover wax and herb with a spoon and bury it under a healthy tree or bin it; recycle the clean jar, and burn the paper safely in a fireproof bowl or tear it up and compost it.
chant:
Blue as river, calm as sky,
ease and strength be standing by.
Hands of healers, steady, wise;
mend and rest and gently rise.
intention: I send steady, loving support to this healing, alongside the care of skilled medical hands.
timing: Start on a Sunday or Monday, during a waxing moon if possible, or simply when care begins.
bestTime: Any season, during a hospital stay, treatment or recovery.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; if you must stop, snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray, at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Glass-jar candles can crack when hot: keep them on a heatproof surface, never in a window or near drafts, and never let them burn dry; stop when about half an inch of wax remains. Hospitals do not allow open flames, so burn it at home, never at the bedside of someone on oxygen. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands afterward and never use oils on broken skin. Herbs go only into holes away from the wick, as dry herbs can flare. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, never put glitter, paper or plastic on the candle, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire (smother it with a lid instead). Let wax cool completely before handling and never pour hot wax down a drain. This spell supports and never replaces medical care; keep following your doctor's advice. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, so keep them out of the room while the candle burns and until it has aired out. Lavender is mildly toxic to cats and dogs if eaten.

name: Waning Moon Notched Habit-Breaking Candle
description: Notched or 'marked' candles are a common folk technique: the candle is divided into sections and one section is burned each night, so the work unfolds over several days. In this version, the waning moon's shrinking light carries a habit away a little more each night. It pairs well with practical steps such as support groups, apps or a doctor's help.

ingredients.item: Black or brown chime candle, about 4 inches (or a black taper for a longer working)
Chime holder on a heatproof plate
Rue or Hyssop, dried and finely ground
Toothpick or blunt knife for notching

steps: Cleanse the candle by wiping it with a cloth dampened in salt water while naming the habit you are releasing.
Mark the candle into seven roughly equal sections with shallow notches, carving away from your hand, and carve the name of the habit near the top.
Dress the candle with Banishing Oil, stroking from the top down toward the base to push the habit away, keeping oil off the wick and the top half inch; wipe off the excess and wash your hands.
Set the candle in its holder on the plate, and sprinkle the ground Rue or Hyssop in a ring on the plate around the base.
Hold the Obsidian, light the candle, and say the chant while you watch the flame.
Let only one section burn each night, staying with it, then snuff it and write one sentence in the notebook about how you resisted the habit that day.
Close the working on the last night: let the final section burn down while you watch, then snuff any remaining flame and say, 'It is gone, and I am free.'
howToUse: Burn one notch a night through the waning moon, beginning about a week before the new moon. When finished and cool, scrape the leftover wax and the herb ring into a paper bag and put it in an outside trash bin off your property, and do not bring it back into the house. Keep the Obsidian in your pocket as a reminder through the next moon.
chant:
Moon that wanes and flame that falls,
loose the habit's grip and calls.
Notch by notch it burns away;
I walk free from day to day.
intention: With every night of the waning moon, I release this habit and grow stronger without it.
timing: Begin seven nights before the new moon; Saturday is a good start.
bestTime: Any season; autumn and the turn of the year are natural times to let go.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; if you must stop, snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray, at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands afterward and never use oils on broken skin. Dried herbs near a flame are a real fire risk: keep them as a light dusting on the lower part only or in a ring on the plate, watch the candle the whole time, and keep a snuffer or lid and a cup of water nearby. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, never put glitter, paper or plastic on the candle, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire (smother it with a lid instead). Let wax cool completely before handling and never pour hot wax down a drain. Rue can cause blistering skin rashes when skin that touched it meets sunlight, so handle it with gloves, wash your hands, and avoid it if pregnant; use Hyssop instead if unsure. This spell supports, and does not replace, medical or professional help for addiction or harmful habits. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, so keep them out of the room while the candle burns and until it has aired out. Keep Rue away from pets; it is harmful if chewed.

name: Nine-Tealight Cleansing Grid
description: Nine is a number of completion in many European folk charms, which often repeat words or knots nine times. In this working, nine white tealights are set in a three-by-three grid on a single tray, lit in a set order, to clear a home or person after a hard stretch. Keeping all nine on one tray makes the grid easy to watch and quick to snuff.

ingredients.item: White tealight candles in metal cups
Large heatproof tray or metal baking sheet, at least 12 x 12 inches
Jinx Removing Oil or Uncrossing Oil
Long-reach lighter and a candle snuffer

steps: Cleanse the tray with salt water and dry it, then lift each tealight out of its cup and wipe it clean.
Carve a small equal-armed cross or an X into the top of each tealight around the wick, carving away from your hand.
Dress each tealight by rubbing one drop of oil onto its side, away from the wick, put them back in their cups, and wash your hands.
Arrange the tealights in three rows of three, at least 3 inches apart, on the tray, and set the quartz in the center tealight's place or just outside the grid if space is tight.
Scatter the salt and Rosemary lightly over the tray between the cups, keeping it out of the cups themselves.
Using the long-reach lighter, light the candles from the top left, row by row, saying one line of the chant (or 'Clear and clean') with each of the nine.
Sit with the grid for at least 30 minutes while picturing grime and heaviness lifting from you and your home, then close by snuffing all nine with the snuffer in reverse order.
howToUse: Relight the grid in attended sessions until the tealights are spent, which takes about four hours in total. Let everything cool completely, then pop out the leftover wax discs, sweep them up with the salt and herb, and put them in an outdoor trash bin; recycle the metal cups. Open a window for a few minutes afterward to let the old air out.
chant:
One for the door and two for the floor,
three for the walls and four for the halls,
five for the heart and six for each part,
seven the air, eight the stair,
nine makes it whole and clears every soul.
intention: I clear myself and my home of every heavy, stale and unwanted energy, complete and whole.
timing: Saturday or Sunday, during a waning moon for removal or a full moon for brightening.
bestTime: Spring cleaning season, the New Year, or after illness or conflict.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; if you must stop, snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray, at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Nine flames make a lot of heat: keep the tealights at least 3 inches apart so they do not heat each other and flare, never reach across lit candles, and use a long-reach lighter. Set the tray on a stable heatproof surface, not on a tablecloth. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands afterward and never use oils on broken skin. Dried herbs near a flame are a real fire risk: keep them as a light dusting on the lower part only or in a ring on the plate, watch the candle the whole time, and keep a snuffer or lid and a cup of water nearby. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, never put glitter, paper or plastic on the candle, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire (smother it with a lid instead). Let wax cool completely before handling and never pour hot wax down a drain. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep the tray well out of reach; salt is harmful to pets if licked up, and tealights burn paws and noses. Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, so keep them out of the room while the candle burns and until it has aired out.

name: White Candle and Water Glass for Ancestors
description: Setting a clear glass of water beside a white candle is a widespread way of honoring the dead in Spiritist, Caribbean and Latin American home practice, as well as in many modern ancestor altars; the water is said to refresh and draw spirits, and the light guides them. This is a simple weekly honoring that can be done at any time of year, with no special holiday required. It is for loving, well-meaning ancestors only.

ingredients.item: White taper or white pillar candle, 6-10 inches
Ancestor Oil (or 1 tsp Olive Oil with 1 drop Frankincense Essential Oil)

ingredients.amount: a few grains on the plate

ingredients.item: A photo or written name of an ancestor

steps: Cleanse the space and candle by wiping both with a cloth dampened in fresh water, and wash your own hands and face.
Carve the name, initials or family surname of the ancestor you are honoring into the candle, carving away from your hand.
Dress the candle with Ancestor Oil from the base upward toward the middle, keeping oil off the wick and the top half inch; wipe off the excess and wash your hands.
Set the candle on its plate, place the glass of fresh water beside it about 4 inches away, and lean the photo or name against the glass, not against the candle.
If using Myrrh, sprinkle a few grains on the plate near, but not touching, the candle base as an offering of scent.
Light the candle, greet your ancestors by name, say the chant, and then simply talk to them about your week, or sit in silence.
After 20 to 60 minutes, close by thanking them; snuff the candle, and say, 'Go in peace and come in love.' Change the water every week.
howToUse: Relight the candle once a week for your visit until it is used up, and replace the water each time, pouring the old water onto the ground outdoors rather than drinking it. When the candle is finished and cool, wrap the leftover wax in a cloth and keep it in a box with family keepsakes, or bury it in a garden or near a tree in their memory.
chant:
Light for those who came before,
water for the open door.
Blood and bone and name I keep;
rest in love, and gently sleep.
intention: I honor my loving ancestors with light and fresh water and welcome their guidance.
timing: Monday or the same evening each week; any moon phase.
bestTime: All year; especially around birthdays and anniversaries of passing.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; if you must stop, snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray, at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Keep the photo and any paper well away from the flame, at least 4 inches from the candle. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands afterward and never use oils on broken skin. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, never put glitter, paper or plastic on the candle, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire (smother it with a lid instead). Let wax cool completely before handling and never pour hot wax down a drain. Myrrh resin should stay on the plate, never on the candle, and only a few grains. The water is an offering only: Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep flames, dressing oils and herbs away from pets; cats are especially sensitive to essential oils, so keep them out of the room while the candle burns and until it has aired out. Keep pets from drinking the offering water.

name: Peaceful Passing Candle for a Beloved Pet
description: Lighting a candle for someone who is dying or has died is one of the oldest and most widespread human customs, and many people now do the same for their animal companions. This gentle working honors a pet who is nearing the end of life or has recently passed, wishing them peace and freedom from pain and giving you a quiet place for grief. It is not a substitute for veterinary care or a vet's advice about comfort and end-of-life decisions.

ingredients.item: Pale blue, lavender or white pillar candle, about 3 x 4 inches
Your pet's collar, tag or a photo

steps: Cleanse the candle by holding it in your hands and breathing gently over it, remembering a happy moment with your pet.
Carve your pet's name and a small paw print or heart into the side of the candle, carving away from your hand.
Dress the candle with a few drops of plain Olive Oil from the base upward toward the middle, keeping oil off the wick and the top half inch; wipe off the excess and wash your hands.
Set the pillar on the plate, scatter the Rose petals in a ring on the plate around the base, and place the collar, tag or photo and the Rose Quartz at least 4 inches from the flame.
If your pet is still with you, light the candle in a different room from where they rest, so the flame and scent stay away from them.
Light the candle, say the chant softly, and speak to your pet, thanking them for the love and the years you shared.
When you are ready, close by snuffing the flame and saying, 'Go gently, friend; you are loved.' Relight it whenever you wish to remember them.
howToUse: Burn it in quiet sessions over the days of their passing and after, as often as feels right; there is no wrong way to grieve. When the candle is spent and cool, you can bury the leftover wax with the rose petals at the place where your pet is laid to rest or beneath a favorite plant, or keep a small piece in a memory box with the collar or tag. Reach out to friends, your vet, or a pet-loss support line if grief feels heavy.
chant:
Soft of paw and warm of heart,
love remains though we must part.
Run in peace through fields of light;
sleep, my friend, and rest tonight.
intention: I wish my beloved companion a peaceful passing, free of pain and wrapped in love.
timing: Any day or hour it is needed; a waning or dark moon suits endings.
bestTime: Whenever the time comes; anniversaries of the loss.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or burning while you sleep; if you must stop, snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it at the next session. Use a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray, at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Animals at the end of life may be weak or confused and should be kept well away from flames and wax. Use plain, unscented oil only for this spell, since essential oils and scented smoke can affect sick animals. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, since too much oil can make the flame flare; wash your hands afterward and never use oils on broken skin. Ventilate the room against smoke and soot, never put glitter, paper or plastic on the candle, and never throw water on hot wax or a wax fire (smother it with a lid instead). Let wax cool completely before handling and never pour hot wax down a drain. Keep petals on the plate, never on the candle. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Burn the candle in a room the pets cannot enter, never near a sick or elderly animal, and keep other pets in the household away from the flame and petals. Avoid essential oils entirely here; cats and birds are especially sensitive to scented vapors.
